title: Psalms Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 4.

questions.question: Who is the psalm addressed to in Psalms 4?
questions.explanation: The psalm is specifically addressed to the chief Musician as stated in Psalms 4:1.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do when he calls upon Him?
questions.explanation: David asks God to 'Hear me when I call' in Psalms 4:1.

questions.question: What has the LORD done for David when he was in distress?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress' in Psalms 4:1.

questions.question: True or False: David expresses a desire for the LORD to have mercy upon him.
questions.explanation: David indeed asks for mercy in Psalms 4:1, stating 'have mercy upon me'.

questions.question: What question does David pose to the sons of men in Psalms 4?
options: How long will you seek after God?
How long will you turn my glory into shame?
How long will you follow vanity?
How long will you love righteousness?
questions.correctAnswer: How long will you turn my glory into shame?
questions.explanation: David asks this question directly in Psalms 4:2.

questions.question: According to Psalms 4:3, who has the LORD set apart for Himself?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states 'the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself' in Psalms 4:3.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will ignore those who call unto Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:3 states 'the LORD will hear when I call unto him', indicating that He will not ignore calls.

questions.question: What does David encourage people to do in Psalms 4:4?
options: Stand in awe and sin not
questions.correctAnswer: Stand in awe and sin not
questions.explanation: David instructs to 'Stand in awe, and sin not' in Psalms 4:4.

questions.question: What should one commune with, according to Psalms 4:4?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs to 'commune with your own heart upon your bed' in Psalms 4:4.

questions.question: True or False: David advises to trust in the LORD in Psalms 4:5.
questions.explanation: David encourages the act of putting trust in the LORD as stated in Psalms 4:5.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to lift up in Psalms 4:6?
questions.explanation: David requests 'LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us' in Psalms 4:6.

questions.question: In Psalms 4, what does David mention as bringing gladness to his heart?
questions.explanation: David notes that the gladness he feels is 'more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased' in Psalms 4:7.

questions.question: What does David express about his ability to sleep in Psalms 4:8?
questions.explanation: David states 'I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep' in Psalms 4:8.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD makes David dwell in safety.
questions.explanation: David confirms that 'for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety' in Psalms 4:8.

questions.question: In Psalms 4, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Stand in awe, and sin not
questions.explanation: The first instruction given by David is to 'Hear me when I call' in Psalms 4:1.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should one do when communing with their own heart, according to Psalms 4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:4 instructs to 'commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still', emphasizing the importance of quiet reflection and stillness before God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 4:5, what should one offer?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:5 specifically mentions to 'Offer the sacrifices of righteousness', indicating that God values righteousness over mere offerings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 4:6 suggest about seeking good?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:6 states that 'There be many that say, Who will shew us any good?', highlighting a common human struggle to find goodness.

questions.question: What is the response to those who turn glory into shame, according to David?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 4:1, David calls upon God for help amid the shame he experiences, showing reliance on divine support.

questions.question: What does Psalms 4:3 say about the godly?
options: They are set apart by the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: They are set apart by the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:3 states, 'the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself', affirming that God values and protects the godly.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express in Psalms 4:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:7 reflects the psalmist's joy, stating, 'Thou hast put gladness in my heart', showing the blessings of God during difficult times.

questions.question: In Psalms 4:1, what does the psalmist ask God to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:1 directly asks God to 'hear me when I call', indicating a deep reliance on God for assistance.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about trust in the Lord in Psalms 4:5?
options: Put your trust in the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Put your trust in the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:5 encourages believers to 'put your trust in the LORD', reinforcing the need for faith.

questions.question: How does Psalms 4:4 connect with Psalms 4:5 regarding behavior?
options: Stand in awe and trust in the Lord
Stand in fear and offer sacrifices
Commune with others and ignore God
questions.correctAnswer: Stand in awe and trust in the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:4 advises to 'Stand in awe, and sin not', which sets the stage for the following instruction in Psalms 4:5 to trust in God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 4:8, the Lord makes the psalmist dwell in safety.
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:8 states, 'for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety', indicating that true safety comes from the Lord.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 4:6 questions if anyone will show us any good.
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:6 poses the question, 'Who will shew us any good?', reflecting a common human concern about goodness in the world.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist encourages silence and reflection as a response to distress in Psalms 4:4.
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:4 advises to 'commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still', promoting reflection during distress.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 4.

questions.question: What emotion does the psalmist express in Psalms 4:7 when reflecting on God's blessings?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Gladness' because Psalms 4:7 states, 'Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased,' indicating a deep joy that surpasses material wealth.

questions.question: According to Psalms 4:3, who does the LORD set apart for Himself?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:3 states, 'But know that the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself,' highlighting that those who are godly are chosen by God.

questions.question: In Psalms 4:6, what does the psalmist request from the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us,' indicating a desire for God's presence and guidance.

questions.question: What is the primary theme expressed in Psalms 4:8 about the psalmist's state of mind?
questions.explanation: Psalms 4:8 says, 'I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety,' emphasizing the tranquility found in trust in the LORD.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Stand in awe, and sin not' in Psalms 4:4 suggest about the nature of reverence towards God?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Stand in awe, and sin not' indicates a call to maintain a respectful and reverent attitude toward God, as stated in Psalms 4:4.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of calling upon God in distress found in Psalms 4:1?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:13 states, 'For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved,' which resonates with the theme of seeking God in times of trouble as seen in Psalms 4:1.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist claims in Psalms 4:5 that sacrifices should be offered in righteousness.
questions.explanation: True. Psalms 4:5 states, 'Offer the sacrifices of righteousness,' implying that sacrifices must be made with integrity and righteousness.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in the phrase 'commune with your own heart upon your bed' in Psalms 4:4?
questions.explanation: The phrase evokes a vivid image of self-reflection and contemplation, making it a prime example of imagery in Psalms 4:4.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the 'vanity' mentioned in Psalms 4:2?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 4:2, the psalmist critiques the love of vanity and seeking after leasing, which implies a pursuit of falsehood or deception.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 4:7 indicates that the psalmist has gladness in his heart due to material wealth.
questions.explanation: False. The gladness expressed in Psalms 4:7 is contrasted with material wealth, indicating it comes from God rather than from corn and wine.

questions.question: What does the term 'Neginoth' in the title of this psalm likely refer to?
questions.explanation: The term 'Neginoth' refers to stringed instruments, indicating that this psalm was intended to be sung or played musically.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage emphasizes God's protection, similar to the assurance in Psalms 4:8?
questions.explanation: Psalm 91:1-2 states that those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty, echoing the safety theme found in Psalms 4:8.

questions.question: The phrase 'put your trust in the LORD' in Psalms 4:5 emphasizes what aspect of faith?
questions.explanation: The instruction to 'put your trust in the LORD' highlights a reliance and confidence in God's character and promises, as mentioned in Psalms 4:5.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David ask God in his prayer in Psalms 4:1?
questions.explanation: David asks God to hear him when he calls, indicating his reliance on God for support during distress (Psalms 4:1).

questions.question: In Psalms 4:2, what does David address to the sons of men?
options: Their turning of glory into shame
questions.correctAnswer: Their turning of glory into shame
questions.explanation: David questions how long the sons of men will turn his glory into shame, highlighting their actions against him (Psalms 4:2).

questions.question: According to Psalms 4:3, who does the LORD set apart for Himself?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD sets apart the godly for Himself, emphasizing His special relationship with the righteous (Psalms 4:3).

questions.question: What does David encourage people to do in Psalms 4:4?
options: Stand in awe and sin not
questions.correctAnswer: Stand in awe and sin not
questions.explanation: David instructs to stand in awe and sin not, suggesting a posture of reverence before God (Psalms 4:4).

questions.question: What are the 'sacrifices of righteousness' mentioned in Psalms 4:5?
questions.explanation: The sacrifices of righteousness refer to the ethical and moral conduct expected of believers (Psalms 4:5).

questions.question: What does David request from the LORD in Psalms 4:6?
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD to lift up the light of His countenance upon them, seeking divine favor and guidance (Psalms 4:6).

questions.question: How does David express his joy in Psalms 4:7?
options: By receiving God's gladness in his heart
questions.correctAnswer: By receiving God's gladness in his heart
questions.explanation: David states that the gladness God has put in his heart surpasses even the joy experienced during times of abundance (Psalms 4:7).

questions.question: What does David declare about his peace in Psalms 4:8?
options: He will find peace in riches
He will find peace in friendships
He will lay down in peace and sleep
He will find peace through his enemies' defeat
questions.correctAnswer: He will lay down in peace and sleep
questions.explanation: David expresses that he will rest peacefully, recognizing that the LORD provides safety (Psalms 4:8).

questions.question: What doctrine about divine righteousness is demonstrated in Psalms 4:1?
questions.explanation: David appeals to God's righteousness, indicating that God is actively engaged in responding to the prayers of the distressed (Psalms 4:1).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Psalms 4:3?
questions.explanation: The setting apart of the godly implies God's holiness and His commitment to those who are righteous (Psalms 4:3).

questions.question: What aspect of human nature is revealed in Psalms 4:2?
options: The inclination to vanity and dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: The inclination to vanity and dishonesty
questions.explanation: David highlights the tendency of humanity to pursue vanity and falsehood, which leads to shame (Psalms 4:2).

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 4:5 and Psalms 4:6 convey about trust in God?
options: Trust in God accompanies righteous living
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God accompanies righteous living
questions.explanation: The verses emphasize that offering righteousness and trusting God are interconnected aspects of faith (Psalms 4:5-6).

questions.question: What combined insight do Psalms 4:4 and Psalms 4:8 provide about peace and sin?
options: Sin can be ignored for peace
questions.explanation: Standing in awe and not sinning is linked to the peace that comes from God, showing the relationship between moral conduct and inner peace (Psalms 4:4-8).

questions.question: What does the skeptic claim regarding divine silence in distress? What does Psalms 4:1-2 actually teach?
options: God responds to cries for help
questions.correctAnswer: God responds to cries for help
questions.explanation: Though skeptics may claim divine silence, David's call for God to hear him illustrates the belief that God is responsive, especially in times of distress (Psalms 4:1-2).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is illustrated through the gladness mentioned in Psalms 4:7?
questions.explanation: The gladness placed in David's heart by God illustrates the divine attribute of joy, emphasizing God's ability to provide spiritual happiness (Psalms 4:7).
